cohort: Pregnant rats were exposed to nitrofen, and their fetuses were harvested at 18 and 21 days postconception and assigned to control, nitrofen-exposed without congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH), and CDH groups.
finding: Nitrofen exposure led to early cardiac impairment, with CDH fetuses exhibiting increased ventricle maximum diameter, decreased minimum diameter, increased interventricular septal thickness, myocardial disarray, and a high density of mitotic myocytes at midgestation and term pregnancy.
gest_age: Exposure at 9.5d postconception (dpc); fetuses harvested at +18 and +21dpc (midgestation and term pregnancy for rats).
